places.name: Sydney Opera House
places.ai_summary: The Sydney Opera House is an iconic architectural masterpiece and a UNESCO World Heritage site. It hosts world-class performances and offers guided tours.
places.place_tip: Book a guided tour to explore the history and architecture of the Opera House.

attribution.title: 2024 Royal Visit Sydney (2)
attribution.author: NSW Government
attribution.description: Sydney Opera House was lit with a royal photo montage on Friday, 18 October 2024, to celebrate the arrival of The King and Queen to Australia.

places.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
places.ai_summary: The Sydney Harbour Bridge is a steel arch bridge that offers breathtaking views of the city. Visitors can climb the bridge or enjoy a leisurely walk across it.
places.place_tip: Try the BridgeClimb experience for panoramic views of Sydney.
places.address: Sydney Harbour Bridge, Sydney NSW, Australia

places.name: Bondi Beach
places.ai_summary: Bondi Beach is one of Australia's most famous beaches, known for its golden sands and surf culture. It's a great spot for swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying beachside cafes.
places.place_tip: Visit the Bondi Icebergs Club for a swim in the ocean pool.

places.name: Blue Mountains National Park
places.ai_summary: A UNESCO World Heritage site, Blue Mountains National Park is known for its stunning scenery, including the famous Three Sisters rock formation. It's a popular destination for hiking and nature walks.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May, September to November
places.place_tip: Take the Scenic Railway or Scenic Skyway for breathtaking views.
places.address: Blue Mountains National Park, NSW, Australia

places.name: Taronga Zoo Sydney
places.ai_summary: Taronga Zoo is a short ferry ride from Circular Quay and is home to over 4,000 animals. The zoo focuses on conservation and offers a range of exhibits and shows.
places.place_tip: Visit the Australian Walkabout section for a close encounter with kangaroos and koalas.
places.address: Bradleys Head Rd, Mosman NSW 2088, Australia

places.name: The Rocks
places.ai_summary: The Rocks is a historic area of Sydney, featuring cobblestone streets, historic buildings, and a vibrant market. It's a great place to explore Sydney's colonial past.
places.place_tip: Visit the Rocks Markets on weekends for unique souvenirs and food.

places.name: Darling Harbour
places.ai_summary: Darling Harbour is a bustling waterfront area with shops, restaurants, and attractions like the SEA LIFE Sydney Aquarium and the Australian National Maritime Museum.
places.place_tip: Check out the Darling Harbour precinct for a variety of dining options.

places.name: Royal Botanic Garden Sydney
places.ai_summary: The Royal Botanic Garden is a large public garden with a diverse range of plants, walking paths, and scenic views of the Sydney Opera House and Harbour Bridge.
places.place_tip: Join a guided tour to learn about the diverse plant species and garden history.
places.address: Mrs Macquaries Rd, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia

places.name: Hunter Valley Wine Region
places.ai_summary: The Hunter Valley is one of Australia's premier wine regions, known for its vineyards, wineries, and gourmet food. It's a popular destination for wine tasting and tours.
places.place_tip: Consider a hot air balloon ride for a unique view of the vineyards.
places.advanced_booking: Recommended for winery tours and hot air balloon rides

places.name: Byron Bay
places.ai_summary: Byron Bay is a coastal town known for its beautiful beaches, surfing spots, and vibrant arts scene. It's a popular destination for those seeking a laid-back atmosphere.
places.place_tip: Visit the Cape Byron Lighthouse for stunning views and whale watching (seasonal).

places.name: Sydney Tower Eye
places.ai_summary: The Sydney Tower Eye is the tallest structure in Sydney, offering panoramic views of the city and beyond. The observation deck provides a 360-degree view, and there's a restaurant and bar at the top.
places.place_tip: Visit during sunset for a breathtaking view of the city lights.

places.name: Art Gallery of New South Wales
places.ai_summary: The Art Gallery of New South Wales is one of Australia's leading art museums, featuring an extensive collection of Australian, European, and Asian art. The gallery also hosts temporary exhibitions and events.
places.name_english: Art Gallery of New South Wales
places.place_tip: Check the gallery's schedule for special exhibitions and events.
places.address: Art Gallery Rd, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia

places.name: Hyams Beach (Jervis Bay)
places.ai_summary: Hyams Beach is famous for having some of the whitest sands in the world and crystal-clear waters. It's a popular spot for swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing.
places.place_tip: Arrive early to secure a parking spot and enjoy a quieter beach experience.
places.address: Hyams Beach, Jervis Bay NSW 2540, Australia

places.place_tip: Participate in the animal feeding sessions for a memorable

places.name: Port Stephens
places.ai_summary: Port Stephens is known for its stunning beaches, marine life, and the Tomaree Head National Park. It's a great destination for dolphin watching, snorkeling, and hiking.

opening_hours.notes: Dolphin watching tours operate during the day.

places.place_tip: Take a dolphin watching cruise for a chance to see these amazing animals up close.

places.name: Manly Beach
places.ai_summary: Manly Beach is famous for its relaxed atmosphere, surf beaches, and scenic walks. It's a popular destination for both locals and tourists.
places.place_tip: Walk the Manly to Spit Bridge coastal trail for stunning views.

places.name: Australian Museum
places.ai_summary: The Australian Museum is the oldest museum in Australia, featuring a vast range of exhibits related to natural history, anthropology, and indigenous cultures.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Christmas Day and Good Friday.

places.place_tip: Join a guided tour to learn about the museum's extensive collections.

places.name: Snowy Mountains
places.ai_summary: The Snowy Mountains are known for their stunning alpine scenery, skiing, and snowboarding in winter, and hiking and mountain biking in summer.
places.cost: Varies (free access, fees for some activities)

opening_hours.notes: Ski resort hours vary in winter.

places.best_time_to_visit: June to October (for snow) / November to April (for hiking and biking)
places.place_tip: Visit the Snowy Mountains during winter for skiing or summer for hiking and mountain biking.
places.advanced_booking: Recommended for ski resorts and popular hiking trails

places.name: Lord Howe Island
places.ai_summary: Lord Howe Island is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its stunning natural beauty, including mountains, beaches, and coral reefs. It's a great destination for snorkeling, hiking, and bird watching.
places.cost: Varies (some areas free, fees for activities)
places.place_tip: Explore the island's walking trails for breathtaking views and unique wildlife.
places.advanced_booking: Essential for accommodation and some activities

places.name: Jenolan Caves
places.ai_summary: The Jenolan Caves are one of the world's oldest and most spectacular cave systems, featuring stunning limestone formations and underground rivers. Guided tours are available.
places.place_tip: Wear comfortable shoes and be prepared for a cool temperature inside the caves.
places.address: Jenolan Caves Rd, Jenolan NSW 2780, Australia
